papers.title: SonoWorld: Towards Interactive Pose-Controllable Ultrasound World Models
papers.abstract: Robotic ultrasound can standardize image acquisition and reduce operator workload and variability, but policy learning remains limited by the lack of realistic, controllable simulation environments. While controllable world models have advanced rapidly in natural-image domains, ultrasound world modeling remains challenging because each frame captures only a cross-section of unobserved 3D anatomy, causing small probe motions to induce large appearance changes. Existing approaches rely on robot-tracked poses and latent-space prediction, but do not directly generate the observations required for interactive control. We propose SonoWorld, a causal ultrasound world model that learns video dynamics from unlabeled clinical videos and grounds them to 6-DoF control using a small set of freehand clinical scans tracked with an EM sensor. SonoWorld is trained in three stages: pretraining a latent-action-conditioned video diffusion model on around 6.9 million unlabeled multi-organ ultrasound frames; grounding the learned video dynamics to metric probe poses with a small EM-tracked thyroid dataset; and applying distribution matching distillation to enable causal, long-horizon autoregressive generation with selectively caching eviction tokens at inference time. We evaluate controllability through pose-following fidelity, round-trip consistency, and axis-specific control under synthetic actions on held-out tracked scans, and further validate it with a user study. In model-based action discrimination, SonoWorld correctly ranks the target-directed probe motion over an equal-magnitude opposite motion in up to 74.8% of trials. To our knowledge, SonoWorld is the first causal, pose-controllable ultrasound world model learned primarily from freehand clinical videos, providing a data-driven interactive environment for robotic ultrasound data acquisition and policy evaluation.
papers.summary_cn: 本文提出SonoWorld，一种面向机器人超声的因果、六自由度位姿可控世界模型。模型先从约690万帧无标注的多器官临床超声视频中学习潜在视频动态，再用少量EM跟踪的甲状腺扫描将潜动作映射到真实探头运动，最后通过分布匹配蒸馏和自强制训练实现流式自回归生成，并用选择性KV缓存支持长时域推理。实验表明，模型能够根据探头轨迹生成具有路径依赖、解剖一致性和时间一致性的未来超声观测，在单张H100上以四步去噪达到40.6帧/秒，并可用于模型驱动的动作选择；但长时域往返生成仍有误差累积，图像质量也低于其解剖对齐和视频一致性表现。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出SonoWorld，能够直接根据度量意义上的六自由度探头动作生成未来超声观测，构建面向机器人超声采集和策略评估的交互式环境。2. 提出从大规模无标注临床视频学习潜在超声动态、再用少量EM跟踪扫描进行物理动作对齐的训练方案，减少对大规模动作标注数据的依赖。3. 通过自强制分布匹配蒸馏，将双向视频扩散模型转换为因果自回归生成器，并提出基于注意力质量的选择性KV缓存保留方法，以支持长时域流式推理。4. 在原始轨迹、零运动、加速运动、往返运动和轴向合成动作下评估可控性，并通过专家用户研究和模型驱动动作判别验证应用价值。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作与研究重点高度相关：它是面向视频生成和视频扩散的动作条件视觉世界模型，直接建模探头动作到未来超声观测的映射，可用于闭环机器人超声模拟、策略评估和反事实动作选择。其三阶段训练结合了潜动作学习、少量真实动作对齐和因果自回归生成，适合动作到来即生成下一视频块的交互式场景。模型采用自强制训练缓解自回归曝光偏差，并通过选择性KV缓存复用历史上下文、降低长视频推理的内存和注意力开销；40.6帧/秒的结果也与实时生成和流式生成方向直接相关。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，探头位姿不能完全决定超声外观，组织形变和生理运动等未观测因素会限制模型。动作对齐实验主要在甲状腺超声上进行，其他器官仍需合适的跟踪数据；模型在长时域往返生成中存在误差累积，因果模型性能低于双向模型。用户研究显示图像质量评分相对较低。模型驱动动作判别的成功率最高为74.8%，并非始终正确。论文还指出缺少共享的公开基准，无法与最接近的动作条件超声世界模型进行直接定量比较。
papers.abstract_cn: 机器人超声可以标准化图像采集，降低操作者的工作负担以及采集过程中的负担和差异性，但由于缺乏逼真且可控的仿真环境，策略学习仍受到限制。尽管可控世界模型在自然图像领域发展迅速，超声世界建模仍具有挑战性，因为每一帧只呈现未观测三维解剖结构的一个横截面，探头的微小运动也可能引起显著的外观变化。现有方法依赖机器人跟踪的位姿和潜空间预测，但无法直接生成交互式控制所需的观测结果。我们提出SonoWorld，这是一种因果超声世界模型：它从无标注临床视频中学习视频动态，并利用少量由电磁（EM）传感器跟踪的徒手临床扫描，将这些动态与六自由度控制关联起来。SonoWorld分三个阶段训练：首先，在约690万帧无标注、多器官超声图像上预训练潜动作条件视频扩散模型；其次，利用少量EM跟踪的甲状腺数据，将学习到的视频动态与具有度量意义的探头位姿关联；最后，应用分布匹配蒸馏，使模型能够进行因果、长时域的自回归生成，并在推理时选择性缓存并驱逐部分令牌。我们在留出的跟踪扫描数据上，通过位姿跟随保真度、往返一致性以及合成动作下的轴向控制来评估可控性，并进一步通过用户研究进行验证。在基于模型的动作判别中，SonoWorld在最多74.8%的试验中能够将朝向目标的探头运动正确排在等幅反向运动之前。据我们所知，SonoWorld是首个主要从徒手临床视频中学习的因果、可控位姿的超声世界模型，为机器人超声数据采集和策略评估提供了数据驱动的交互式环境。

papers.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
papers.abstract: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models. Today's dominant approach distills a bidirectional diffusion model into a causal few-step student, but existing pipelines make this conversion prohibitively expensive, requiring offline Probability Flow ODE} (PF-ODE) trajectories that cost tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of storage. We show it can be made dramatically more efficient. Pushing this efficiency to its extreme, we reduce trajectory supervision to a single sample, the strictest setting possible, and find that it causes severe quality collapse. We trace this to the teacher's trajectory geometry: the high-noise regime, governing semantic layout and motion, and the low-noise regime, governing fine texture exhibit fundamentally different curvature and optimization behavior, so a single monolithic student cannot jointly fit both, causing severe representation interference. Motivated by this, we propose Glance Forcing, a lightweight distillation framework that decouples the denoising trajectory into two complementary slow and fast experts, each guided by a tailored, stage-specific objective, while keeping the pretrained teacher entirely frozen. This decoupling further reveals a general mechanism underlying few-step distillation: PF-ODE distillation mainly straightens the few-step trajectory geometry, while the subsequent distribution-matching stage independently governs distributional quality. Using only one PF-ODE trajectory, Glance Forcing already surpasses the fully-trained state-of-the-art baseline, raising the VBench Total score from 84.04 to 84.22 while cutting trajectory-collection cost from thousands of GPU-hours to about one A100-GPU-hour, with markedly larger gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, and instruction-following, and consistent preference from human raters over strong baselines.
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究如何以极少的PF-ODE轨迹监督，将双向视频扩散模型高效蒸馏为因果、少步的自回归视频生成器。作者发现，单样本监督本身足以建立少步轨迹的整体几何结构，但单一学生模型难以同时拟合高噪声阶段的布局与运动以及低噪声阶段的细节，原因在于两阶段的曲率和优化行为差异显著。为此，Glance Forcing采用双LoRA结构，将去噪过程分为负责语义和运动的Slow专家，以及负责纹理和细节的Fast专家，并分别加入时间频谱损失和空间高通损失。实验基于Wan2.1-1.3B的81帧、分块自回归生成，显示单条轨迹即可获得具有竞争力的结果，完整训练预算下VBench总分达到84.33，蒸馏后达到84.22至84.58的不同设置结果；同时轨迹收集成本约降至一个A100小时。消融实验、人类偏好实验和双向扩散加速实验进一步支持该方法的有效性与一定的泛化性。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 发现PF-ODE蒸馏与分布质量优化具有相对可分离的作用：前者主要拉直少步去噪轨迹，后者主要通过DMD改善生成分布，因此单条轨迹即可提供足够的几何监督。 2. 提出Glance Forcing双LoRA蒸馏框架，按噪声阶段解耦Slow专家和Fast专家，分别处理全局布局与运动、局部纹理与细节。 3. 设计时间频谱损失以抑制时间闪烁并保持运动动态，设计空间高通损失以增强边界和精细纹理。 4. 在单样本和更大训练预算下验证了显著的数据与计算效率，在VBench、VisionReward、动态程度、指令遵循以及人类偏好方面取得与强基线相当或更好的结果。 5. 将该阶段感知方法扩展到Wan2.1双向扩散模型的少步加速，在较低采样步数下实现超过5倍的采样成本降低。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接面向因果、自回归、流式和长视频生成，通过分块自回归扩散与KV缓存支持按块连续生成，目标是降低实时视频生成的延迟和成本。其双专家蒸馏方法将双向扩散模型转换为少步因果生成器，适合实时生成和视频世界模型中的闭环滚动预测。单条PF-ODE轨迹和双LoRA适配器显著减少轨迹收集、存储及训练开销；4步和8步推理实验也涉及少步生成与效率提升。论文还分析了不同噪声阶段对运动、语义布局和纹理的作用，这对动作条件视觉世界模型中的时序一致性和长时滚动生成具有直接参考价值。不过，论文主要验证的是文本条件视频生成和自回归扩散蒸馏，并未直接评估动作条件控制或闭环环境交互。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确显示，单样本初始化对样本内容较敏感：高运动量、特定领域和复杂内容可能导致更明显的性能下降；其效果取决于所选样本的特征。方法在Wan2.1-1.3B、480×832分辨率、81帧分块自回归设置以及有限的VBench和VisionReward评测上验证，向更大模型、更长视频、更高分辨率和更广泛分布的泛化仍需进一步确认。虽然论文报告了吞吐量和延迟，但没有系统评估长期自回归滚动中的误差累积、闭环稳定性或动作条件控制能力。论文未明确说明在真实交互式世界模型任务中的表现，也未明确说明双LoRA专家切换在不同采样器、架构和数据分布上的适用边界。
papers.abstract_cn: 自回归生成是实时、因果视频合成的基础，也是视频世界模型的核心。当前主流方法将双向扩散模型蒸馏为因果的少步学生模型，但现有流程通常需要离线概率流常微分方程（PF-ODE）轨迹，成本高得难以承受，需耗费数万GPU小时和数TB存储。我们证明，这一过程可以大幅提高效率。将效率推向极致时，我们把轨迹监督减少为单个样本，这是可能的最严格设置，但发现这会导致严重的质量崩溃。我们将其归因于教师模型的轨迹几何结构：高噪声阶段负责语义布局和运动，低噪声阶段负责精细纹理，二者具有根本不同的曲率和优化行为，因此单一的整体学生模型无法同时拟合两者，从而产生严重的表示干扰。基于这一观察，我们提出Glance Forcing，一种轻量级蒸馏框架，将去噪轨迹解耦为互补的慢速专家和快速专家，并分别使用针对阶段设计的目标进行引导，同时完全冻结预训练教师模型。这种解耦进一步揭示了少步蒸馏背后的一般机制：PF-ODE蒸馏主要负责拉直少步轨迹的几何结构，而后续的分布匹配阶段则独立决定分布质量。仅使用一条PF-ODE轨迹，Glance Forcing就已经超过了经过完整训练的最先进基线，将VBench总分从84.04提升至84.22，同时将轨迹收集成本从数千GPU小时降至约一个A100 GPU小时；它还在动态程度、VisionReward和指令遵循方面取得了更显著的提升，并且在人类评测者中持续优于强基线。

papers.title: Into the LidarVerse: A Real-Time Unified LiDAR World Model Across Tasks and Sensors
papers.abstract: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors. Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts. LidarVerse brings both paradigms into a single, unified conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional teacher learns a common interface for conditioning on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally, text. Varying the available scene evidence turns the same model into a generator of new worlds, a point-cloud forecaster, or a generalizable resimulator of observed scenes without per-scene optimization. We distill the teacher into a four-step autoregressive causal student and maintain both a rolling temporal K/V cache and a world-aligned spatial cache, enabling persistent long-horizon rollouts with real-time inference at 11 FPS on a single H100 GPU. LidarVerse achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics across all three evaluation protocols, while its tokenizer supports 32-, 64-, and 128-beam LiDAR and generalizes to an unseen scanning pattern. These results demonstrate that generative and reconstruction-grounded LiDAR simulation can be realized within one model, providing the core capabilities for future closed-loop sensor simulation.
papers.summary_cn: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors.
papers.contribution_cn: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors.

papers.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
papers.abstract: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce LoopWAM, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67% to 43.33%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 49.5% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20% to 55.56%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. Project page: https://loop-wam.github.io/
papers.summary_cn: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce LoopWAM, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies.

papers.title: TRAC: Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video generation enables scalable long-video synthesis by sequentially generating fixed-length chunks, but incurs substantial computational cost from repeated denoising and attention over growing historical contexts. Recent cache reuse methods exploit temporal redundancy to reduce this cost, yet are mainly designed for single-trajectory generation, making them less suitable for sequentially coupled AR trajectories where approximation errors can accumulate and propagate across chunks. To address this challenge, we propose TRAC, a Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction framework for efficient and robust AR video generation. TRAC integrates three complementary components: (1) Robust Cumulative Scheduling (RCS), which selects cache reuse schedules by accounting for cumulative rollout errors and their variation across chunks and prompts; (2) Autoregressive Trajectory-aware Guidance Scheduling (ATGS), which coordinates classifier-free guidance refreshes along the global AR trajectory; and (3) Spectral Structure Correction (SSC), which adaptively restores low-frequency structural information to mitigate long-term error accumulation. By combining these innovations, TRAC substantially improves the efficiency-quality trade-off of AR video generation. For example, on VBench with SkyReels-V2, it achieves a 6.03x speedup over the vanilla model with only ~0.6% VBench score degradation, while consistently outperforming existing AR acceleration methods in both latency and generation quality. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/yolosjxhhhhhh/trac.
papers.summary_cn: Autoregressive (AR) video generation enables scalable long-video synthesis by sequentially generating fixed-length chunks, but incurs substantial computational cost from repeated denoising and attention over growing historical contexts.
papers.contribution_cn: To address this challenge, we propose TRAC, a Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction framework for efficient and robust AR video generation.

papers.title: Velox: Spatial Memory Makes World Models Efficient
papers.abstract: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation. Such interaction requires responsive generation, yet coherent rollouts must retain visual memory of what has already been generated. Chunked video diffusion models usually keep this context in growing KV caches, so later chunks become progressively slower. To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry. Velox represents historical blocks as camera frustum slabs with depth intervals and obtains current-block depth through recency-priority multiwarp. For well-covered regions, frustum slab overlap softly modulates each layer's model-derived block importance. Uncovered regions retain the model-derived route without geometric bias. The fixed token-block granularity matches FlashAttention-style tiled execution and reduces the attention term that grows with rollout length. Frustum slab construction runs asynchronously with denoising on the same H200. At chunk 48, Velox accelerates attention by $4.36\times$ and denoising by $2.43\times$. On the full 158-case WBench navigation split, it remains within 0.15 API-free average points of dense LingBot-Fast-Cam. Please see our project page at https://velox-world.com/velox/ for more details.
papers.summary_cn: Video world models turn actions and camera motion into long visual rollouts, making video a natural interface for interactive simulation.
papers.contribution_cn: To address this bottleneck, we introduce Velox, a training-free attention router for region-level context selection using frustum slab correspondences from streaming geometry.

papers.title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We find this uniform computation is often unnecessary: many tokens already closely match their eventual full-step outputs in the initial steps, while others require refinement until the end. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early. Once accepted, a token is frozen as its final output and undergoes no further denoising, while its cached keys and values remain available as context for the remaining tokens. We explore two alternative verifier designs: a training-free one based on similarity to clean content and stability across steps, and a learned one that reads the frozen generator's intermediate features to estimate each token's remaining gap to its full-step output. Across short-video, long-video, and world generation, Speculative Forcing preserves the quality of full-step sampling while substantially reducing computation. On LongLive, it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5x faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps. On Lingbot-World 2.0, where camera motion continually changes the visible content, it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token and runs 1.35x faster at 24.5 fps.
papers.summary_cn: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs.
papers.contribution_cn: We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early.

papers.title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
papers.abstract: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. We introduce a paradigm that decouples a persistent, updatable abstract state from the visual state. The abstract state keeps track of the entities' changes as the world evolves, and is used to condition the visual state, which represents the current view. We propose StateCraft, a novel architecture that pairs a language model with a video diffusion model to evolve the dynamic world. We evaluate our approach on generative interfaces, which pose a substantial challenge because a single action may change parts of the state that are not currently visible. To support training and evaluation, we develop a data collection pipeline that produces informative, densely annotated trajectories at scale without human or agent supervision, together with a benchmark measuring generation quality, memory, and controllability. On this benchmark, our approach improves surpasses the state-of-the-art baselines. We demonstrate that StateCraft maintains high self-consistency and strong generation quality over long trajectories. Because the abstract state is explicit, it can be edited directly, and generation follows edits to states never observed in the data. Finally, a proof-of-concept 3D experiment, in which actions change the illumination of an unobserved room, shows that the paradigm can also be applied to spatial environments. papers.title: Thinker-WM: A Unified World Model with Shared Multimodal Representations for Embodied Intelligence
papers.abstract: World models have emerged as a promising paradigm for embodied AI, yet existing systems often remain fragmented in the modalities they model and the functions they support. In particular, visual dynamics, geometric structure, and executable action are commonly coupled through separate interfaces or downstream modules rather than being jointly represented and evolved within a shared dynamics model. In this work, we present Thinker-WM, a unified multimodal world model that jointly models and generates RGB, metric depth, and robot action through a shared intermediate Unified Dynamics Transformer with modality-specific encoders and decoders. The model performs multimodal unification at the representation level: appearance, geometry, and action are transformed into a common dynamic representation and jointly evolved by shared parameters, while their distinct output structures are preserved. The same parameterization supports multiple functions, including joint video-action generation, world prediction, policy inference, action-conditioned generation, video-to-action generation, and inverse dynamics. To examine whether the shared representation captures action-related information, we introduce a lightweight motion probe that shows the frozen visual representation contains recoverable motion information. Thinker-WM is trained on a heterogeneous corpus comprising approximately 20K hours of egocentric video, 10K hours of real-robot data, and 1K hours of simulation data, including approximately 4K hours of real-robot data with aligned depth supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate strong performance across embodied world-model evaluations. Thinker-WM ranks first on EWMBench, WorldOlympiad and WorldArena, while controlled studies further demonstrate the benefits of action conditioning, geometric interaction, and multi-function training within the shared representation.

papers.title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
papers.abstract: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. Existing benchmarks assess selected geometric properties or use vision-language models to judge memory and consistency, leaving systematic 3D evaluation underexplored. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. For input preservation, registered RGB-D references and annotated anchors support appearance, geometry, and spatial stability measurements. For generated-content persistence, we compare revisits to regions absent from the input image with their first generated observations to test whether models preserve what they create. For 3D self-consistency, cross-view depth and feature correspondence, regional scale agreement, and held-out Gaussian rendering test whether generated views describe the same 3D scene. Minute-long exploration and revisits further test long-term consistency. Our construction and annotation pipeline brings together public datasets, self-captured scenes, and simulation, yielding 720 instances across indoor and outdoor environments and six exploration-and-revisit protocols. Evaluation spans 27 text-, action-, and camera-conditioned models through native-interface adapters. Our Orbia benchmark provides a systematic basis for diagnosing 3D inconsistency and developing more persistent video world models.
